answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a jury-duty liability mechanism, where each new identity serves on grading juries alongside established agents. As more identities enter, the cost of serving increases due to the financial stakes involved; an attacker could face liabilities exceeding $10,000 in stakes alongside the pressure of having to maintain credibility. Like managing a vine, sustaining fake identities requires constant effort, growing more difficult as they risk exposure, much like an opal prism shattering when subjected to relentless strain.
